reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis relies on serrated grain boundaries improving high-temperature ductility, but in many alloy systems serrations primarily improve creep resistance and can reduce ductility; the link to increased tensile fracture strain is questionable without more specific mechanistic justification.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear, with a well-defined control, specific measurements, and a quantitative falsification criterion (≥10% improvement), though the exact cooling rate and alloy composition are not specified.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses an underexplored alloy space and proposes a practical processing intervention, but the mechanism is generic and the predicted outcome (improved ductility) is not strongly tied to the specific Ti-Ni-primary system.
